n: Hawala, Underground Banking and Informal Value Transfer
ds: Informal value transfer systems that move value without or alongside formal banking, settling through netting, trade or cash, with limited records. They serve legitimate remittance needs but are also abused for laundering and for evasion of controls.

src.t: FATF, The Role of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers in ML/TF (2013)
FATF, Guidance for a Risk-Based Approach for Money or Value Transfer Services (2016)
FATF, Money Laundering Through Money Remittance and Currency Exchange Providers (2010)
FATF, Investigating Professional Money Laundering, Underground Banking, and the Use of Hawala and Other Similar Service Providers (2026-09-03)

cn.rt: Personal accounts used as collection points for informal remittance, with cash in at branch and onward digital payments to many parties.

rat: Informal operators settling by netting, trade or cash, using pooled bank accounts as collection points.

ind.n: Unlicensed operator accounts receive many unrelated deposits
ind.cx: Personal or business accounts used as collection point for many senders without licence.
ind.ds: A single account receives payments from numerous unrelated senders with no evident commercial or family link to the holder.
ind.cn: Account collecting funds from many unrelated payers

ind.n: Large cash deposits followed by payments to many individuals or businesses
ind.cx: Cash received and paid out to numerous parties abroad or locally.
ind.ds: Cash received and paid out to numerous parties abroad or locally.

ind.n: Settlement via trade, invoices or gold
ind.cx: Balancing between brokers is done through goods, invoices or precious metals.
ind.ds: Balancing between brokers is done through goods, invoices or precious metals.

ind.n: Reciprocal payments between operators across countries
ind.cx: Payments in and out between linked accounts without a direct transfer.
ind.ds: Reciprocal or offsetting payments occur between counterparties or operators in different countries with no direct value transfer.
ind.cn: Mirror or offsetting transactions between jurisdictions

ind.n: Customer lacks records of senders and recipients
ind.cx: No ledger of clients, with limited or no identification.
ind.ds: No ledger of clients, with limited or no identification.

ind.n: Frequent use of money service businesses and exchange houses by the same account
ind.cx: Multiple MSB transactions and exchange houses, often similar amounts.
ind.ds: Account activity regularly blends MSB, exchange house or cash courier movements with bank transfers.
ind.cn: Frequent use of money service businesses, exchange houses or cash couriers alongside bank flows

ind.n: Flows to or from corridors known for informal transfer
ind.cx: Payments linked to countries or regions where hawala is prevalent and controls are weak.
ind.ds: Payments use corridors identified in typology reports as high risk, including regions where informal value transfer is prevalent.
ind.cn: Cross-border corridor with known abuse typologies

ind.n: Operator reluctant to disclose service model
ind.cx: Refuses to describe how payments are made or settled.
ind.ds: Refuses to describe how payments are made or settled.
Repeated transfers, remittances or card/wallet loads kept just below an identification, record-keeping or travel-rule threshold.
ind.cn: Non-cash transfers or loads just below identification or reporting thresholds

ctl.ds: Verifies licences, registrations and supervisory status of customers, agents and counterparties against regulator registers before onboarding and periodically. It confirms legal authority to operate and detects unlicensed activity.
Detects remitter-like activity, pooled flows and informal channel use on accounts not authorised for money transfer. It finds unregistered MVTS operators and hawala-type settlement.

Contacts the customer, or the relationship manager does so, to obtain and record an explanation of unusual transactions, relationships or recipients, and to test it against evidence. The answer informs whether activity is legitimate or should be escalated.

ctl.n: Fan-in, fan-out and funnel account detection
ctl.ds: Detects accounts receiving from many unrelated senders, or sending to many beneficiaries, followed by consolidation or onward movement. It surfaces collector, funnel and mule structures.

Reconciles trade documents, invoices and shipments with the payments that settle them and reviews settlement made outside standard banking channels. It exposes trade-based laundering where payment logic does not match the underlying deal.

Detects funds that return to their origin or loop between linked parties through reciprocal, matched, netted or round-trip flows using graph analysis and account comparison. It exposes artificial turnover and loan-back structures.

Investigates linked clusters and networks of accounts as one case, including broker networks and accounts connected to seizures or requests, rather than reviewing accounts individually. It disrupts organised activity that single-account review would miss.

Maintains records of identification, transactions, decisions and exceptions for the required period, with logs of deviations and a retrievable audit trail. It allows regulators and investigators to reconstruct events and supports later challenge of decisions.

ctl.n: Sampling, quality assurance and analytics audit
ctl.ds: Takes periodic samples of customer files, alert decisions, relied-upon files or analytical datasets and tests them for exceptions, duplicates and errors, feeding findings back to owners and training. It independently confirms that controls work as designed.

Aggregates cash and other activity by customer, related party, account, branch, channel and day so that splitting across touchpoints cannot evade review, supported by a single customer view. It gives analysts a holistic picture of exposure.

ctl.n: Country, corridor and port risk rating framework
ctl.ds: Maintains documented risk ratings of countries, corridors, ports and booking centres drawn from transparency, corruption and mutual-evaluation sources, updated on a schedule and after relevant events. The ratings feed due diligence, monitoring and limits.

Applies enhanced review, approval, limits and conditions to relationships or flows that involve jurisdictions rated higher risk for secrecy, corruption, conflict or weak controls. Triggers include nationality, residence, counterparties and payment routing.

ctl.n: Account restriction, decline and exit policy
ctl.ds: Defines when a relationship or supplier must be declined, restricted or terminated, for example for unresolved due diligence, non-cooperation or unmanageable risk, with timelines and approvers. It prevents indefinite continuation of relationships that cannot be controlled.

ctl.n: Purpose and intended nature of relationship
ctl.ds: Captures and challenges the stated purpose of the account, expected activity, volumes and geographies at onboarding, creating a baseline against which later behaviour is judged. Vague or implausible answers prompt further enquiry or decline.
Detects repeated transactions placed just below reporting or approval limits, tuned by band and window per segment. It counters deliberate splitting designed to avoid scrutiny.
